_comment: Sensor-aware, sharded, windowed multi-workload for the K1 demo Gantt. Every net is tied to a real sensor path in the flying drone demo, and its PERIOD is its real sampling/firing rate (record_sensor_demo.py fires: CTRL 50Hz, NAV 50Hz, YOLO ~4.17Hz, camera 10Hz). YOLOv8n is the DOMINATING network: 98 dispatches, ~184ms single-core, so the scheduler must SPLIT (shard) it across harts to meet its detection deadline -- machine_combination_mode=shard + topo_tag_override=false lets the solver pick a per-dispatch core width from the measured 1/2/4/8-hart profiles. enable_impls additionally lets the transformer vision-head (ffn/attn) linears (M=128, above the M=10.1 IME/RVV crossover) run on the cluster-0 IME MAC unit. num_instances are RT-driven (floor(window/period)) not arbitrary. ffn_block/attn_block are a ViNT-class vision-transformer STAND-IN over the FPV camera until FusedSensorViT/ViNT/DepthAnythingV3-small are compiled (requests_to_a/009,010).
_shard_comment: Only yolov8_nano_64x96, dronet, ffn_block have multi-hart profiles, so only they can shard; mlp_control/fused_full/attn_block have no multi-hart CSV, so their multi-hart combos are excluded and they stay single-core automatically. topo_tag_override=false is required so each shard block is costed from its own N-hart profile (topo_0_1_2_3 etc.), not the single-core one.
_edges_comment: MUST stay empty for the fused_full->mlp_control relationship: a precedence edge would force control to WAIT for nav, deleting the staleness phenomenon. The sensor/perception freshness relationship lives in freshness_edges and is evaluated post-hoc.

freshness_edges._comment: Control consumes the nav steer command; if nav is stale the controller acts on old guidance. Window = 2x nav period (20ms) as the age ceiling.
